To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the instruction to construct relational stimuli beyond simple name-giving, in training on concatenated conditional discriminations, facilitates the subsequent emergence of transitive responding.

the construction of supplemental relational stimuli is necessary for the derivation of relations in multiple conditional discrimination, and that this construction can be induced by an instructional variable.
the construction of supplemental relational stimuli is necessary for the derivation of complex stimulus relations and is a function of instructional variables.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of self-constructed relational stimulus elements in the derivation of complex relationships such as transitivity.

the problem-solving process that is required to derive relations among stimulus elements, and the extent to which the construction of relational stimuli may be a critical component of such problem solving.
the construction of relational stimuli by subjects as an essential part of the solution of complex problems, and with the control of such problem-solving by the instructions given to the subject.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the construction of relational stimuli is a critical component of the process of relational derivation, but that the construction of such stimuli can be either spontaneous or instructed.
the construction of supplementary relational stimulation is a necessary condition for error-free derivation of complex relations among stimulus elements.
the derivation of relations is a problem solving process controlled by self-structured relational stimuli.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, as a problem-solving process, relational derivation is under the control of the construction of supplementary stimuli.
the derivation of emergent relations is controlled by the self-construction of relational stimuli.

the construction of relational stimuli is a necessary and sufficient condition for the solution of complex problems, such that the derivation of relations in multiple conditional discrimination tests may be viewed as a form of Skinnerian problem solving.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the construction of relational stimuli is not only a means to the end of solving a problem, but it is also a necessary condition for problem solving.
the construction of relational stimuli may be a key factor in the derivation of complex stimulus relations.
relational stimuli can be spontaneously constructed by the learner and that such constructed stimuli can control the learner's behavior in subsequent tasks.
